title.en: Progressive asset streaming with explicit stage ownership

summary: Package a scene as an independently valid shell plus prioritized asset stages, with abort, retry, identity and replacement rules for every stage.
objective: The first useful view appears from a bounded shell, later stages replace placeholders without identity or transform jumps, and cancellation or partial failure leaves a coherent fallback.
intent_signals: show a useful shell before details
example_prompts: Deliver a large architectural scene in useful stages with a static fallback.
Load a product shell first, then replace named assemblies without camera jumps.
Make scene navigation cancel obsolete asset requests and dispose late results.
not_for: A single offline asset that must be opened atomically.
Claims about load time or frame rate without a target network and device measurement.

principles: A stage is a complete application state, not an arbitrary byte boundary: it names visible content, stable anchors, dependencies, fallback and promotion conditions.

Progressive packaging is application orchestration around transportable assets. Core glTF does not promise that an arbitrary GLB becomes meaningfully renderable before its required content is available.
Cancellation has two owners: abort outstanding fetch work where the API exposes an AbortSignal, and reject or dispose results that finish after their stage generation became obsolete.
implementation: In Blender, publish a lightweight shell collection with final world units, pivots, bounds, cameras and stable logical IDs; export detail stages as independently inspectable glTF/GLB assets whose attachment transforms are declared against shell anchors.

Create a versioned stage manifest containing asset URL, content hash, priority, dependencies, anchor ID, placeholder policy, required extensions/decoders and optional/fatal failure class. Do not infer identity from load order or transient scene-child indices.

In Three.js, keep one generation token and cancellation scope per requested scene state. Fetch abortable resources with the token, parse only current results, attach them under their declared anchors, atomically transfer semantic/UI ownership, and dispose placeholders or stale late results exactly once.

Expose shell, loading, degraded and complete states. Retry only the failed stage and its dependents; a missing optional detail retains its placeholder while a failed required structural stage selects the declared fallback.
observable_checks: Cold start reaches the shell using only stage-zero files; no later stage is required to frame the camera or explain the loading state.
Completing stages in reversed network order yields the same final logical IDs, transforms and visible hierarchy as manifest order.
Navigation during a large request aborts exposed fetch work; any non-abortable late completion is rejected by generation and its owned resources are disposed without entering the scene.
One optional-stage failure produces the declared degraded view and retry replaces only that stage; one required-stage failure selects the declared fallback instead of an empty canvas.

creative_affordances: Stage order can follow narrative reveal, spatial proximity or interaction intent.
Placeholders may be graphic, diagrammatic or low-detail as long as promotion rules are explicit.
known_limits: This profile does not claim HTTP, GLB or GLTFLoader alone provides semantic progressive rendering.
No network, decoder, load, cancellation, disposal or performance observation was run.

claims.statement: The Fetch Standard connects a Request signal to fetch abort steps: aborting rejects a still-pending fetch promise, cancels a readable request body, and errors a readable response body; invoking abort after the fetch promise is already fulfilled does not retroactively reject that promise.
claims.scope: WHATWG Fetch living standard read 2026-09-08; this describes fetch-owned promises and body streams, not decoder, parser or Three.js loader cancellation.

source_refs.locator: Fetch method abort steps and “To abort a fetch() call”

claims.statement: The current Three.js GLTFLoader documentation exposes load callbacks for completion, progress and error plus parse/parseAsync and loader plugin registration; it does not document semantic stage partitioning or a general load-abort handle.
claims.scope: Live unversioned Three.js GLTFLoader API read 2026-09-08; installed revision and any wrapper-specific cancellation must be verified.

source_refs.locator: load, parse, parseAsync and register methods
